lesson.explanation: A context window is the amount of text an AI model can see and consider at once, like its working memory. Let's walk through a small example. Suppose the window holds about 40 words, and you have sent a long chat where your first message said, "My dog is named Biscuit and I need a birthday poem for him." Later you write, "Now make it funnier." Step one: the model receives the whole conversation as one request. Step two: it checks whether everything fits inside its window. Step three: if the earlier messages push past the limit, the oldest text may be cut off. Step four: if the naming message was dropped, the model no longer knows the dog's name and may write a poem about a generic pet. The lesson: anything outside the window is effectively invisible to the model. To avoid this, repeat key details in your newest message or keep long conversations focused. Sources note that when a prompt or document exceeds the window, information can be lost, so plan what the model needs to see.

resources.title: What is a context window? | IBM
resources.snippet: An LLM’s context window can be thought of as the equivalent of its working memory. It determines how long of a conversation it can carry out without forgetting details from earlier in the exchange. It also determines the maximum size of documents or code samples that it can process at once. questions.prompt: A 500-word English paragraph uses more than 500 tokens in a model's context window. Why?
options: Tokens are often shorter than words, so one word can span several
The window also stores a saved copy of the words
Tokens are counted per sentence rather than per word
Each word is counted twice in the window

questions.prompt: You need a model to analyze a 60-page report, but the chat's context window is too small to hold all of it. What is the best approach?
options: Assume the first pages stay visible while the rest is dropped
Count pages as words and assume the report fits
Expect the model to recall the report from last week's chat
Split the report and send the key sections that fit the window

questions.prompt: A support bot answers a customer's question correctly on day one. On day two, in a new session with no earlier text, it ignores the order number the customer gave on day one. What is the most likely cause?
options: The day-one text is no longer in the context window
The order number used more words than the bot's limit
Earlier messages stay in view but were misread
The bot saved the order number in permanent memory and forgot it
